# SB-1017 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P2, line P2-L2
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Hazard description
Airborne dust generated during abrasive blasting operations within the P2-L2 area presents inhalation and secondary exposure risks to operators, maintenance personnel, and adjacent work zones. Dust from blasting contains particulate metal, spent abrasive, and surface coatings that can be respirable and can deposit on surfaces where it becomes re-entrainable. Short-term exposure can cause irritation of the eyes, nose, throat, and lungs; prolonged or repeated exposure to metal-containing dusts can contribute to chronic respiratory conditions and increase the risk of systemic toxicity depending on composition. Secondary risks include reduced visibility, contamination of controls and sensors, and ignition of pyrophoric fines where applicable. The risk is highest during active blasting, clean-out of blast cabinets and enclosures, and when performing machine maintenance that disturbs accumulated deposits.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to blasting activities and associated dust control when performed in proximity to line P2-L2 and to equipment listed below:
- Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill EQ-P2-L2-RR03
- Blasting enclosures, portable blast cabinets, and blast recovery systems serving P2-L2
- Adjacent conveyors, ventilation intakes, and local control stations in the P2-L2 work cell

Required controls
Engineering controls
- Use enclosed blasting booths or temporary containment to limit dust spread beyond the immediate blasting area. Enclosures must interface with building ventilation to create negative pressure relative to adjacent workspaces and must discharge through filtration compliant with plant filtration practice (see SOP-P2-L2-03).
- Install and maintain local extraction at the point of blast media impact for processes that cannot be fully enclosed. Extraction inlet placement should capture generated dust before it becomes broadly airborne.
- Ensure blast recovery and media handling systems are sealed to prevent fugitive emissions during transfer and media handling.

Administrative controls
- Plan blasting work to minimize personnel in adjacent workspaces during operations. Post visible signage at the boundary of the blasting zone while operations are active.
- Sequence cleaning and housekeeping to remove settled dust using wet methods or HEPA-filtered vacuuming rather than brushing or compressed air to prevent re-entrainment.
- Coordinate blasting and ring rolling operations to avoid simultaneous activities that could increase personnel exposure in the P2-L2 area.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
- Respiratory protection selection shall follow the plant respiratory program and be based on task-specific hazard assessment. Where mechanical ventilation and enclosure controls are not sufficient to maintain exposures below acceptable levels per plant policy, use assigned respirators and cartridges appropriate for particulate challenge (see SOP-P2-L2-03).
- Eye and face protection, protective clothing, and gloves should be used to prevent dermal contact and eye irritation from dust.

Maintenance-specific controls and rationale
- During maintenance on EQ-P2-L2-RR03 and related systems, isolate and dampen potentially contaminated systems prior to opening enclosures or accessing internals to reduce airborne re-entrainment of settled dust.
- Where bolted assemblies are exposed to blast-generated dust, clean joint faces with HEPA-vacuuming and wipe-down before disassembly. This reduces abrasive particles that can accelerate wear or create secondary dust clouds.
- Critical fastener torque must be verified after maintenance that exposes structural or load-bearing connections on ring rolling equipment. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 620 N·m. Use calibrated torque equipment documented in maintenance records per MM-P2-L2-RR03.

Examples and application
- Example 1: For a scheduled blast cleaning of a ring surface adjacent to EQ-P2-L2-RR03, the blasting area was set up with a temporary containment tent and a dedicated HEPA-filtered exhaust. Extraction inlet was positioned at the immediate impact zone, and a dedicated HEPA vacuum was used to remove settled dust before technicians entered to perform inspection. This prevented dust migration into the mill gap and avoided respiratory exposures in adjacent work benches.
- Example 2: During maintenance on a blast recovery hopper, personnel followed the administrative sequence of lockout/tagout, HEPA vacuum cleanup of the hopper interior, and then opening for inspection. Surfaces were wiped and replaced filters were verified in the local extraction system before resuming blasting operations.

Records to keep
- Blasting activity log: document date, location (P2-L2), work order number, personnel involved, presence and type of containment, type of abrasive media used, and verification that enclosure/ventilation was functioning. Retain according to plant record retention practice; reference SOP-P2-L2-03 for required log fields.
- Maintenance records: include post-maintenance torque verification for relevant fasteners. For EQ-P2-L2-RR03, record the mandrel clamp bolt torque verification entry showing 620 N·m and the calibrated tool used. Cross-reference these entries to MM-P2-L2-RR03 work orders.
- Air monitoring and filter change records: document any personal or area air monitoring performed during blasting events, and retention or disposal records for used HEPA filters or collected media.
- Training and competency records: document that personnel performing blasting, clean-up, and maintenance have completed required training modules and practical assessments per SOP-P2-L2-03.

Step rationale
Controls emphasize elimination and containment of dust at source to reduce reliance on PPE. Engineering controls such as enclosures and local extraction are the most effective means of reducing airborne particulate spread. Administrative measures, including sequencing and documented cleanup methods, prevent secondary exposures. The specific maintenance requirement to verify mandrel clamp bolt torque for EQ-P2-L2-RR03 at 620 N·m ensures mechanical integrity after activities that may loosen fasteners due to vibration or disassembly; documenting this action provides traceability in case of downstream issues. Refer to MM-P2-L2-RR03 for maintenance procedures and SB-1049 for related airborne particulate guidance.

Related documents
MM-P2-L2-RR03
SB-1049
SOP-P2-L2-03

Effective date
Effective date: Upon release of Rev B

Action required
Supervisors and maintenance planners in P2-L2 must incorporate these controls into job plans and permit-to-work documents immediately. Compliance will be audited during routine safety walks and maintenance reviews.
